fact: The Bank of Ghana revoked Zeepay's Dedicated Electronic Money Issuer licence on 14 July 2026 under Section 13 of the Payment Systems and Services Act, 2019 (Act 987), showing the Act in force.

Zeepay Ghana, a fintech company, held a Dedicated Electronic Money Issuer licence from the Bank of Ghana under the Payment Systems and Services Act, 2019 (Act 987), which the Bank revoked on 14 July 2026 over inadequate cash backing of e-money.

Digital Policy Alert states Ghana implemented the Payment Systems and Services Act in February 2020, setting licensing requirements for payment service providers and electronic money issuers (document published 2025-04-02).

Digital Policy Alert states the Payment Systems and Services Act (February 2020) requires payment service providers and electronic money issuers to obtain a Bank of Ghana licence, assessed on financial stability, technology, anti-money-laundering compliance and consumer protection.
iAfrikan says Ghana mandated mobile money interoperability in 2018, without naming the rule.

The article describes the Payment Systems and Services Act, 2019 (Act 987) as the law governing mobile money, electronic money issuers and payment service providers, with complaint-handling duties for them.
